_comment: Canonical system namespace for every feature (Dropbox /saves, SD backup, the Media catalogue). The keys of `systems` (below) = REAL Batocera system folder names (1:1 mirror of /userdata/saves/<system>, so batocera<->Dropbox needs no reconciliation). A system is an architecture, not a node: a node can host several. Pluto owns this list; the @dropbox cloud picker shows it, and the Vue app imports it. `nodeConsoles` = which consoles each node can host (many-to-many: wii runs wii + gamecube; dc + vmu both serve dreamcast; ws covers wswan mono + wswanc colour). '*' = emulator host, serves any console. A node may map to a system not yet in `systems` -- add it there to name it.
_statePatternsComment: Savestate extensions per console, for cards that write them. Kept SEPARATE from savePatterns because the two go to different places: saves are canonical and shared (/saves/<console>), states are emulator/hardware-locked and never interchange, so they are siloed per node (/states/<console>/<node>). A console listed here with an empty array means 'this card may write states but we have not yet seen one' -- fill it in from a real `scan` of the card rather than guessing, the way the save extensions were derived from batocera's actual output.
_saveFormatsComment: How a file in a node's save dir is CLASSIFIED, lifted out of api.py (was hardcoded there). 'state*' = emulator savestates: hardware-locked, never interchange, so they go to /states/<console>/<node>/ instead of the canonical /saves. stateContains is a SUBSTRING test because batocera numbers them .state1/.state2/...; stateSuffixes is an endswith test (.png = a savestate's thumbnail). skipDirs/skipExts are not save data at all and never leave the node.
_savePatternsComment: File extensions that ARE a save, per console -- derived from what batocera actually produced in /saves (surveyed 2026-08-24), not guessed. Used to pull saves off a whole SD card by pattern instead of hard-coding each card's directory layout: walk the card, take what matches, wherever it lives. A pattern is EITHER an extension ('.srm') or an exact filename ('ss_save.bin', matched case-insensitively) -- SAROO forced the latter: its saves are SS_SAVE.BIN (internal backup RAM) and SS_MEMS.BIN (the emulated 8MB cartridge), both observed on the real card 2026-08-24, while '.bin' on that same card is also 3962 disc images totalling 117GB plus the firmware blobs. DELIBERATELY OMITTED: '.bin' as a bare extension. It is a real save extension inside batocera's saves dir (saturn yabasanshiro/backup.bin) but on a raw SD card '.bin' is also what disc images are called, so matching it there would drag in whole games. Add a card-specific extension here once a scan of that card shows what it really writes. Dreamcast is absent on purpose: its saves arrive per-file from the VMU reader and carry no extension.
_systemsComment: Per-SYSTEM facts shared by every feature (saves, SD backup, the Media catalogue). Keys are Batocera folder names, same namespace as `consoles`. brand = manufacturer, the grid groups families by it; name = display name; icon = avatar key in pluto/src/composables/useIcons.ts (omit = lettered tile); header = which ROM header reader identifies its games (pluto/api/modules/catalogue/headers.py formats: megadrive, sms, gba, saturn, dreamcast; omit = match by filename only); thumbnails = libretro-thumbnails repo for box art (github.com/libretro-thumbnails); emulator = key into `emulators` overriding `defaultEmulator` for this system. Several systems can share a format (mastersystem + gamegear both read the SMS header).
_emulatorsComment: Desktop emulators on the Lab (macOS) for the Media drawer's Play button, like a file association: `defaultEmulator` for every system, systems.<x>.emulator overrides it. app = the .app name for `open -a`. args = launch arguments with {rom} for the ROM path, passed via `open -a <app> --args ...`; omit to hand the ROM over as a document (OpenEmu imports and starts it). Remote start on real consoles will be per node, not here.
_filtersComment: Metadata fields a system's Media page offers to Group by (libretro-database: genre, developer, publisher, year). defaultFilters for every system; systems.<x>.filters overrides it. A field with no values for that system's games is hidden anyway, so this only narrows or reorders.
_ignoreSystemsComment: Batocera folders the catalogue never lists: ports and apps Batocera restores on every boot (deleting them doesn't stick). DOS returns on the EEE PC as its own node.
